svg.title: RIEMANN-MASULLO-DIAGRAMS D3 — Chapter 3 · Ch03_IdelicZeta, declaration by declaration
svg.desc: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 990 declarations of the 86 items on C3, each with its kind, file, line and state; 70 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Posters: M1, what the targets rest on · M2, the steps with no known repair · M3, the paper by depth · M4, every chapter · M5, the refutations. Names, items, files, entries and posters are links, underlined under the pointer: a card's title or a Lean name opens the source at the pin.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: How to read it. The expansion of C3's cards, in the same order: one block per item, its heading opening the card. First the declarations whose docstring states how the Lean departs from the print, each with its Deviation: line quoted from the Lean source (Apache-2.0), then every declaration of the item. A name opens its line at the

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: pin. A declaration's state is read from the terms: open when it uses sorryAx, resting when something open is below it. That a declaration states what its Deviation: line says is the docstring's claim, not checked here.

g.text: The formula evaluates ordinary derivatives on the test function. With the printed scaling D = (2πi)⁻¹∂ₓ, the degree-one residue is +4πi times (Df)(0). For the distribution derivative defined by negative transpose it is −4πi times (Dδ₀)(f), as in (3.3.2.7). Equation (3.3.2.20) evaluates D on the test. The degree-one residue of the separate factor ρ for the library's Fourier convention is +4πi,
